assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT gave the first controllable, non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and in practice the workhorse for Mott transitions, heavy fermions and correlated oxides. It is original, conceptually clear and tied to real materials through DFT+DMFT, which is close to my own methods work and to spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt and Metzner introduced the large-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar (with Krauth and Rozenberg) mapped it onto the Anderson impurity problem and built DMFT. Kotliar also drove the DFT+DMFT extension. Metzner is not among the credited names and is a real omission; the supplied trio is a defensible but imperfect configuration.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent use, with widely reproduced results and routine comparison with photoemission and optical spectra. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Walter Metzner's role is not representable in the supplied credit list and credit between the 1989 limit and the 1992 to 1996 mapping needs careful weighing.
Some committee members may see DMFT as a method rather than a discovery of a physical phenomenon.
Quantitative reliability for low-dimensional or strongly non-local correlations is limited; I rely on memory for the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the whole field of moire quantum matter. This is a genuine new platform for correlated states, in the spirit of the surprises quantum mechanics keeps delivering in materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of flat bands (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group (Cao et al., 2018) realised and measured the correlated phases. Yuan Cao, the first author of the experiments, is not credited and the allocation would be a sensitive question. The three supplied names form a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently reproduced across many groups and extended to other moire systems. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid. Recognition is timely, arguably a little early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated insulators are unsettled.
Other early theory contributions (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Suarez Morell et al.) are not in the credit list.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the later coherent-tunnelling giant TMR in MgO junctions are a clear physical effect with large technological consequences for read heads and magnetic memory, and they build directly on spin-dependent tunnelling that theory (Butler, Mathon) explained from first principles. The link between quantum mechanics and practical devices is strong.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira and colleagues showed giant TMR in MgO. Yuasa and Djayaprawira are not in the credited names and Parkin's GMR connection to the 2007 prize is relevant. The trio is plausible but the MgO part is incompletely covered by the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and large-scale deployment; interpretation via symmetry-filtered tunnelling is well verified by band-structure theory. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue, though it may be seen as an incremental follow-on to the GMR prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may count against it.
MgO-barrier credit sits with people outside the supplied names.
I am relying on memory for precise priority dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe observation of helical edge transport, established a new class of quantum matter protected by time-reversal symmetry. Very influential on band-structure theory and spectroscopy, and verified in a quantitative manner.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and the QSH model; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum well and Konig et al. (Molenkamp) observed it; Hasan and others realised 3D topological insulators. Not all key people are creditable here, and Zhang is deceased. The Kane, Mele, Molenkamp choice leaves out the 3D line and Hasan.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by transport and photoemission in many materials, with a mature theory. Quantized edge transport is cleaner in the QAH variant than in QSH. Timing is reasonable though the 2016 topological-phase prize may be seen as covering part of the territory.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases.
Credit between 2D QSH and 3D topological insulators is split and the supplied list cannot cover both.
Edge conduction in HgTe is not perfectly quantised in longer devices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism is a third collinear magnetic class with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, a genuinely new symmetry-based concept in my own field, relevant to spintronics and sustainable, rare-earth-free magnetic materials. It was found through symmetry analysis and first-principles calculation and then confirmed in spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Smejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth gave the 2022 classification and conceptual framing; related earlier ideas exist (e.g. Hayami, Yanagi, Kusunose; Yuan and others; Naka et al.). Experimental realization in MnTe and CrSb by ARPES involves further groups not credited. Attribution is not yet settled.
assessment.maturity: The field is only a few years old. ARPES and other confirmations in MnTe, CrSb and elsewhere are encouraging but device relevance and the full scope are unproven. This is probably premature for 2026 but very promising.
uncertainties: Priority claims from the Japanese and other groups remain contested.
Experimental confirmation is limited to a few materials and breadth of impact is untested.
Possible premature recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting through dissociation of dislocations and disclinations, with the hexatic phase, is a deep and original statistical-physics result, extending the topological-defect ideas honoured in 2016. It was confirmed by simulation and by colloidal and other experiments.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson predicted the hexatic phase (1978), with Young's independent contributions; Kosterlitz and Thouless already received the 2016 prize and Kosterlitz is not on the list. The trio forms a natural and relatively clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long experimental and numerical confirmation, although the exact melting scenario varies between systems. Recognition would be very late, but clearly deserved on the science.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the work as sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize.
Details of the transition order differ across real systems.
Some contributors may be deceased or the history be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to photons and underpins most superconducting quantum computers. It is a clean quantum-mechanical discovery with major technological reach and it follows naturally on the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed it in 2004; Wallraff et al. demonstrated strong coupling the same year. Girvin is a fourth essential name, so with a three-person limit a genuine contribution is left out.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and heavily used. Close association with the 2025 prize might make a quick successor unlikely, and some may see it as engineering infrastructure.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize.
A four-person credit that cannot be fully honoured.
Distinction between physics discovery and technology platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV centres in diamond made a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale quantum sensor, with wide impact in physics and biology. The physics is clear and validated, and it fits spectroscopy-based experimental practice.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko did the 1997 single-centre detection and coherent control, while Lukin and others brought quantum registers and sensing applications. The credit is plausible but overlaps with B010 and others (Awschalom, Hanson not in this entry).
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced worldwide with commercial sensors. Maturity is good, although sensing is still developing and the work is partly an enabling technology.
uncertainties: Overlap with other solid-state spin-qubit candidates and unclear distinction in credit.
Whether sensing applications are mature enough to be a stand-alone discovery.
Precise priority details are from memory.
